## Claims
- [source-backed] The paper records the minimality of both Theorem \(5.4\) generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) as conjectural and reports finite computer verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1497-1502]
- [source-backed] For a graded connected algebra and a graded module bounded below, homogeneous generators are equivalent to generators of \(M/\Lambda_+M\); inclusion-minimal generating families correspond to inclusion-minimal spanning families of that quotient. [source-2, lines 1520-1533]
- [proved] Minimality does not imply that indecomposables are free of the same rank, even for a torsion-free underlying abelian module. Let \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(M=(2,x)\subset R\). Then \(\{2,x\}\) is an inclusion-minimal homogeneous \(R\)-generating family, \(M\) is torsion-free over \(\mathbb Z\), and
  \[
  M/R_+M=M/xM\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2.
  \]
- [proved] Minimality also does not determine rational rank. For \(M=R=\mathbb Z[x]\), the homogeneous family \(\{2,3\}\) is inclusion-minimal and generates \(R\), but
  \[
  M/R_+M=R/xR\cong\mathbb Z,
  \]
  of rank \(1\), although the family has cardinality \(2\).
- [proved] If \(M\) is a finite-rank free abelian group and \(N\subseteq M\), then
  \[
  M/N\cong\mathbb Z^N
  \]
  holds if and only if \(N\) is saturated in \(M\) and
  \[
  \dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl((M\otimes\mathbb Q)/(N\otimes\mathbb Q)\bigr)=N.
  \]
- [conjectural] For the proposed \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), a direct proof must separately establish saturation of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) and the indicated rational dimension; minimality alone cannot provide either conclusion.

## Strategy
Put \(N=\Lambda_+J_v\). The saturation criterion follows because \(M/N\) is torsion-free exactly when
\[
kx\in N,\ k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in N,
\]
and a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group is free. Its rank is computed after tensoring with \(\mathbb Q\).

Thus a viable direct route is:
1. compute \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) over \(\mathbb Q\) and prove dimension \(\binom{a+b}{a}\);
2. prove the integral Pieri/Littlewood--Richardson relation lattice \(\Lambda_+J_v\) is saturated in the Schur lattice of \(J_v\).

The two examples show that neither step follows formally from a minimal generating-family theorem.

## Gaps
No saturation argument or uniform rational-rank computation is supplied for general \(J_v\). Hence this does not prove either the integral indecomposables statement or minimality of the transposed family.

## Next
Seek a uniform unimodular or Smith-normal-form description of the complete positive-degree Pieri relation lattice; saturation is the precise integral obstruction.
